title: Lifting a finite family of maps from finite-projective open-site stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $T\subseteq V$ opens and $x\in T$. Let $I$ be a finite set and let $M_q,N_q$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O_V$-modules on the slice site, for $q\in I$. Suppose each $M_q$ is a retract of a finite free sheaf: for some $m_q\in\mathbf N$ there are $\iota_q:M_q\to\mathcal O_V^{m_q}$ and $\pi_q:\mathcal O_V^{m_q}\to M_q$ with $\iota_q\pi_q=1_{M_q}$ (the termwise retraction condition of [def-pc-perfect-complex]). Write $F$ for the open module stalk functor at $x$ [def-sc-open-module-stalk-functor]. For arbitrary maps $h_q:F(M_q)\to F(N_q)$ there exist an open $Z\subseteq T$ containing $x$, a natural isomorphism $e:R_{Z,V}S_Z\cong F$ on module sheaves, and maps $k_q:R_{Z,V}(M_q)\to R_{Z,V}(N_q)$ such that $S_Z(k_q)=e_{M_q}h_qe_{N_q}^{-1}$ for every $q\in I$. Targets are arbitrary; no complex, boundedness, degree relation or differential equation occurs.

proof.text: Use the retractions to precompose each stalk map with the projection from a finite free sheaf. Such a map is specified by finitely many target-stalk vectors. Equivalently finite-presentation internal Hom gives a germ of a local sheaf morphism. Represent these finitely many germs on neighbourhoods inside T and intersect the neighbourhoods; finiteness of I and each rank makes this a neighbourhood of x. This is the representative argument in Tag 01CP, requiring no finite-presentation condition on the targets.

Restrict the chosen representatives to the intersection and precompose with the restricted source inclusions. On stalks their composite equals the prescribed map because inclusion followed by projection is the identity. The canonical restriction-stalk comparison on module sheaves, using the open-subscheme equivalence and restriction of scalars, is natural in every sheaf; its naturality converts the germ agreement to the stated conjugation identity. Empty index families and rank-zero sources use T and zero maps.

theorem exists_finite_projective_open_stalk_maps_lift
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (V : X.Opens) (x : X) (hxV : x ∈ V)
    (T : X.Opens) (hTV : T ≤ V) (hxT : x ∈ T)
    (I : Type u) [Finite I]
    (M N : I → SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))
    (hM : ∀ q, ∃ m : ℕ,
      ∃ (ι : M q ⟶ SheafOfModules.free
          (R := (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V) (ULift.{u} (Fin m)))
        (π : SheafOfModules.free
          (R := (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V) (ULift.{u} (Fin m)) ⟶ M q),
        ι ≫ π = 𝟙 (M q))
    (h : ∀ q, (openModuleStalkFunctor X V ⟨x, hxV⟩).obj (M q) ⟶
      (openModuleStalkFunctor X V ⟨x, hxV⟩).obj (N q)) :
    ∃ (Z : X.Opens) (hZT : Z ≤ T) (hxZ : x ∈ Z),
      let R := SheafOfModules.overMap (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
        (homOfLE (hZT.trans hTV))
      let S := openModuleStalkFunctor X Z ⟨x, hxZ⟩
      let F := openModuleStalkFunctor X V ⟨x, hxV⟩
      ∃ (e : R ⋙ S ≅ F) (k : ∀ q, R.obj (M q) ⟶ R.obj (N q)),
        ∀ q, S.map (k q) = (e.app (M q)).hom ≫ h q ≫ (e.app (N q)).inv
